name: just-enough-quota-bar
description: Claude Code and Codex subscription quota windows in the VS Code status bar. Nothing more.

jeqb.alignment.markdownDescription: Side of the status bar the quota items appear on.

jeqb.missingValue.markdownDescription: Text shown instead of a variable whose value is not available.

jeqb.announced.includeEstimates.markdownDescription: When nothing is announced, show whenreset's estimate of the next reset as `announced.next`, with `announced.kind` set to `estimate`. The estimate is the last reset plus the typical gap, a fixed day that never moves forward; once that day is over, the value is missing.

jeqb.claude.enabled.markdownDescription: Show the Claude quota in the status bar.

jeqb.claude.format.markdownDescription: Format of the Claude status bar text. Python-style: `{5h.pct}`, `{week.reset:%a %H:%M}`, `{{` and `}}` for literal braces; `$(codicon)` icons are kept. Variables: `5h.pct`, `5h.left`, `5h.reset`, `week.pct`, `week.left`, `week.reset`, `banked.count`, `banked.expires`, `announced.next`, `announced.kind`, `announced.last`, `announced.p24`, `announced.p48`, `name`. Each variable with a threshold color becomes its own status bar item.

jeqb.claude.priority.markdownDescription: Priority of the first Claude item; every further item of the format gets one less, so the order of the format is kept. A higher priority is placed further left.

enumDescriptions: whenreset.app, a community tracker of the announced resets. Credited and linked in the tooltip.
No announced reset: the `announced.*` variables stay empty and nothing is fetched.
jeqb.claude.announcedSource.markdownDescription: Where the `announced.*` variables of Claude come from: a community tracker of the global resets the vendor announces, a third party with its own terms. It is only asked while `#jeqb.claude.format#` uses an `announced.*` variable, then every 30 minutes and at most every 5, with an identifying `User-Agent`. When the tracker fails, only the `announced.*` variables are missing.

jeqb.codex.enabled.markdownDescription: Show the Codex quota in the status bar.

jeqb.codex.format.markdownDescription: Format of the Codex status bar text. Python-style: `{5h.pct}`, `{week.reset:%a %H:%M}`, `{{` and `}}` for literal braces; `$(codicon)` icons are kept. Variables: `5h.pct`, `5h.left`, `5h.reset`, `week.pct`, `week.left`, `week.reset`, `banked.count`, `banked.expires`, `announced.next`, `announced.kind`, `announced.last`, `announced.p24`, `announced.p48`, `name`. Each variable with a threshold color becomes its own status bar item.

jeqb.codex.priority.markdownDescription: Priority of the first Codex item; every further item of the format gets one less, so the order of the format is kept. A higher priority is placed further left.

enumDescriptions: whenreset.app, a community tracker of the announced resets. Credited and linked in the tooltip.
codex-reset.com, which covers Codex only and gives no announced time, just `announced.p24`, `announced.p48` and `announced.last`. Credited and linked in the tooltip, as its terms require.
No announced reset: the `announced.*` variables stay empty and nothing is fetched.
jeqb.codex.announcedSource.markdownDescription: Where the `announced.*` variables of Codex come from: a community tracker of the global resets the vendor announces, a third party with its own terms. It is only asked while `#jeqb.codex.format#` uses an `announced.*` variable, then every 30 minutes and at most every 5 (whenreset) or every minute (codex-reset), with an identifying `User-Agent`. When the tracker fails, only the `announced.*` variables are missing.

jeqb.thresholds.markdownDescription: Colors by variable name. Each value is a list of steps evaluated in order; the last matching step wins. Time variables compare the remaining duration.

gte.description: Matches when the value is greater than or equal to this number or duration such as "3d".

gt.description: Matches when the value is greater than this number or duration.

lte.description: Matches when the value is less than or equal to this number or duration such as "90m".

lt.description: Matches when the value is less than this number or duration.

eq.description: Matches when a text variable equals this text.

color.description: Theme color ID such as charts.red, or #rrggbb.

background.description: Status bar background; VS Code only allows warning and error.

jeqb.claude.thresholds.markdownDescription: Claude thresholds; each key replaces the same key of `#jeqb.thresholds#`.

gte.description: Matches when the value is greater than or equal to this number or duration such as "3d".

gt.description: Matches when the value is greater than this number or duration.

lte.description: Matches when the value is less than or equal to this number or duration such as "90m".

lt.description: Matches when the value is less than this number or duration.

eq.description: Matches when a text variable equals this text.

color.description: Theme color ID such as charts.red, or #rrggbb.

background.description: Status bar background; VS Code only allows warning and error.

jeqb.codex.binaryPath.markdownDescription: Path of the `codex` executable used for `codex app-server`. Empty: the first `codex` (on Windows `codex.exe` or `codex.cmd`) on the `PATH`.

enumDescriptions: Use `codex app-server` when the `codex` binary is found, otherwise the probe.
Always ask `codex app-server`. It uses no quota, but needs the `codex` binary.
Always use the probe. It reads `~/.codex/auth.json` and sends a minimal request that uses a small amount of quota.
jeqb.codex.source.markdownDescription: Where the Codex quota comes from. `auto`: `codex app-server` when the `codex` binary is found (it uses no quota), otherwise the probe. `probe` asks the undocumented ChatGPT endpoints with the token of `auth.json` (`$CODEX_HOME` or `~/.codex`) and sends a minimal request, which **uses a small amount of quota** on every run; see `#jeqb.codex.probeIntervalMinutes#`.

jeqb.codex.probeIntervalMinutes.markdownDescription: Minutes between two Codex probe runs. Every run sends a minimal request that **uses a small amount of quota**, so the interval is never shorter than 10 minutes, even if a smaller value is set. Only used when the probe is the Codex source.

lte.description: Matches when the value is less than or equal to this number or duration such as "90m".

lt.description: Matches when the value is less than this number or duration.

eq.description: Matches when a text variable equals this text.

color.description: Theme color ID such as charts.red, or #rrggbb.

background.description: Status bar background; VS Code only allows warning and error.

jeqb.staleColor.markdownDescription: Color of stale data, above every threshold. Theme color ID or `#rrggbb`.
